clue.text: Sarah's performing in the drawing room

parts.note: Sal is a familiar short form of the name Sarah; the 's reads as 'is' joining the pieces
a show that is performing is on, as in 'the play is on'

explanation.surface: Sarah is giving a recital in the drawing room.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Sarah's performing' as 'Sal is on': the possessive look of 'Sarah's' hides 'Sarah is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A salon is an elegant reception room in a grand house, the same thing as a drawing room.

clue.text: Seaweed that is essential for an Australian sheepdog

parts.note: kelp is a large brown seaweed
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for 'that is'

explanation.surface: Seaweed is said to be a vital part of an Australian dog's diet.
explanation.definitionFit: The kelpie is a breed of working dog developed in Australia for herding sheep.

clue.text: Diet fare served in snack bars

definitions.text: Diet fare served in snack bars

parts.words: Diet fare served in snack bars
parts.note: reads as slimming food on a menu, but 'diet fare' can be food eaten around a fast, and snack bars serve quick meals

explanation.definitionFit: Quick ready-made meals such as burgers are the staple of snack bars, while the first word plays on going without food.

clue.text: Some retain a record of correspondence

indicators.note: one word holding the other words inside it is said to retain them

parts.note: any means some, as in 'have you any money?'
a log is a written record, like a ship's log

explanation.surface: Some people keep copies of all their letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retain' puts A plus LOG inside ANY.
explanation.definitionFit: An analogy is a likeness or parallel between two things, which is one sense of correspondence.

clue.text: Upsetting misfortune in a tale is likely to be erroneous

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a fable is a short story, a tale with a moral

indicators.note: in a down clue upsetting turns a word upside down, so the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: ill means misfortune or harm, as in 'ills of the world'

explanation.surface: A tale of misfortune told badly is probably inaccurate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upsetting' turns ILL to LLI, which goes 'in' FABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something capable of making mistakes is prone to error.

clue.text: Rise to meet the challenge

parts.note: to stand up is to rise from a seat

explanation.surface: Get to your feet and face the test.
explanation.definitionFit: To confront or resist something bravely is to meet its challenge head-on.

clue.text: Try hard to avoid using analgesics

definitions.meaning: to make a great effort to do something carefully
humorously, to accept the aches rather than swallow painkillers

explanation.surface: Make an effort not to rely on painkillers.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be very careful and thorough, and taken literally it means putting up with hurt instead of medicating it.

clue.text: Is desperate to get American trousers

definitions.meaning: someone who ... for something longs for it eagerly
in the US, the word for trousers is the same one the British use for underpants

explanation.surface: He badly wants a pair of American trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Panting after something shows eager longing, and in American English the word is the ordinary name for trousers.

clue.text: Right to enter objection when describing raw wine

indicators.note: one letter goes into another word, entering it

parts.note: a but is an objection, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: A complaint is raised about unrefined wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enter' puts R inside BUT. The French word means raw or unrefined, and on a label it describes very dry champagne.
explanation.definitionFit: On sparkling wine labels the word marks the driest style, literally the French for crude or unrefined.

clue.text: Where a wounded pilot has to be transferred

definitions.text: Where a wounded pilot has to be transferred

indicators.note: something wounded is damaged, so the letters of the words that follow are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A pilot hurt in action must be taken for treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wounded' rearranges PILOT and HAS; the whole clue also describes the place itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An injured airman would be moved to a medical centre for treatment, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Irritating telephone call around 1.50

indicators.note: one word goes around another, holding it inside

parts.note: a ring is a phone call, as in 'give me a ring'
in Roman numerals I is one and L is fifty

explanation.surface: An annoying phone call comes at ten to two.
explanation.walkthrough: '1.50' looks like a time or a price; read it as 1 and 50, the Roman numerals I and L, which go inside RING.
explanation.definitionFit: To rile someone is to annoy them, so riling means annoying.

clue.text: Note and second note

parts.note: me (or mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale
a mo is a moment, as in 'wait a mo'

explanation.surface: A note, and then another note.
explanation.definitionFit: A short written message or reminder is a note.

clue.text: Move round to dismiss Jack at the wicket

parts.note: in cricket to get a batsman is to dismiss him
a jack is a sailor, and AB (able seaman) is a sailor too
a batsman dismissed at the wicket is out

explanation.surface: Fielders move position to dismiss the batsman Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket (a British bat-and-ball game) the batsman stands at the wicket; 'get Jack out' means dismiss him.
explanation.definitionFit: To get about is to travel around or circulate, which is moving round.

clue.text: Interrogation cell used as a restaurant

parts.note: a grilling is an intense interrogation, and grill is the noun or verb for it
a cell is a small room

explanation.surface: A police interview cell has been turned into an eating place.
explanation.definitionFit: A grillroom is an eating place specialising in grilled meat, a kind of restaurant.

clue.text: It is featured in vulgar religious mission

indicators.note: one piece appears inside another, as an item is featured in a show

parts.note: crude means vulgar or coarse
'it' is old slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: Something tasteless forms part of a religious campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' as sex appeal (SA) is a crossword favourite; 'featured in' places SA inside CRUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval crusades were military expeditions with a religious aim, and the word now means any zealous campaign.

clue.text: Thank God!

parts.note: reads as an exclamation of relief, but taken literally is an instruction to give thanks before a meal

explanation.definitionFit: Saying a short prayer of thanks before eating is literally thanking God.

clue.text: Privation clearly seen in Paraguay

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: PY is the international vehicle code for Paraguay
overt means open and plainly visible

explanation.surface: Want is evident in the South American country.
explanation.definitionFit: Poverty is a state of want or hardship, the lack of necessities that privation means.

clue.text: How the unwary are caught when spring comes

definitions.text: How the unwary are caught when spring comes

parts.words: How the unwary are caught when spring comes
parts.note: reads as a seasonal remark, but describes people caught unprepared, with spring meaning a jump rather than the season

explanation.definitionFit: To be caught napping or unprepared is the idiom, and a hop is a little spring or jump.

clue.text: Curiously proud to become a social misfit

indicators.note: done curiously, in an odd way, so the letters of the next words come out jumbled

explanation.surface: A proud person ends up an outcast, oddly enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rejects conventional society, or quits school, is an outsider who doesn't fit in.

clue.text: The drama wasn't bad, to be honest

parts.note: a play is a drama for the stage
fair means middling, not bad, as in 'fair to middling'

explanation.surface: The critic thought the production wasn't bad, honestly speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: To act justly and by the rules is to deal honestly with others.

clue.text: Does it follow John?

definitions.meaning: does as in performs or behaves, a verb in the third person
the New Testament book after the Gospel of John

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means performs or behaves, and the Acts of the Apostles come straight after John's Gospel in the Bible.

clue.text: Small bird confronts one monkey in S America

indicators.note: one piece stands in front of the other, facing it

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird such as a blue tit
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A small bird faces down a monkey in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: The titi is a small long-tailed monkey of South American forests.

clue.text: Bishop in examination of ethnic groups

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a trial is an examination or test
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop is being tested on ethnic matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribal describes things belonging to tribes, which are ethnic or kinship groups.

clue.text: Transport French iron on trains

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sits on top of the other

parts.note: fer is the French word for iron
RY is the abbreviation for railway, where trains run

explanation.surface: French iron is carried by rail.
explanation.definitionFit: A ferry is a boat that carries people or vehicles across water, a form of transport.

clue.text: Tedious rubbish which could ruin the deal

parts.note: dry means dull or tedious, as in a dry lecture
rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: Boring nonsense could wreck the business agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' looks like a business agreement; here it is pine or fir timber, which this fungus decays.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry rot is a fungus that decays timber, and deal is softwood planking.

clue.text: Took the chair with bias already established

parts.note: the prefix pre- means beforehand, settled in advance
sided means partial, taking one side, as in one-sided

explanation.surface: The chairman ran the meeting with his mind already made up.
explanation.definitionFit: To preside is to act as chairman of a meeting, so presided means chaired.

clue.text: Nick is without honour

parts.note: without means not having, so it stands for not
CH is the Companion of Honour, a British award

explanation.surface: He's a man lacking in honour.
explanation.walkthrough: CH, Companion of Honour, is a British order.
explanation.definitionFit: A notch is a small V-shaped cut, which is a nick.

clue.text: Sang and acted with affectation

definitions.meaning: literally put on tunes, performed songs
behaved in a snobbish, pretentious way

explanation.definitionFit: Taken literally the phrase means performed songs, and as an idiom it means behaved pretentiously.
